scope.note: Findings are bounded checks of cited primary text, not full original-context certification or authority to publish.

findings.locator: Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 71–73; textual-removal allegation and dialogue
findings.document_finding: Justin accuses some Jewish teachers of omissions from the Septuagint and Trypho asks which scriptures were allegedly removed.
findings.qualification: A contested early Christian allegation is not independent proof of systematic deliberate alteration by later Jewish communities.

findings.locator: Bellarmine, De Romano Pontifice II.30, fifth opinion, translated excerpt
findings.document_finding: Bellarmine argues conditionally that a manifestly heretical pope would cease to be pope; the sedevacantist writer quotes the distinction.
findings.qualification: Neither translation nor conditional resolves whether any living pontiff satisfies the factual and juridical predicate.

findings.locator: Novus Ordo Watch, 2015 reading of Bellarmine and a heretical pope
findings.document_finding: The contemporary sedevacantist proponent contends that manifest heresy and Church membership are incompatible with papal headship.
findings.qualification: The argument is attributed to its actual partisan advocate and not independently judged canonical doctrine.

findings.locator: Joint Liturgical Group institutional history: interdenominational British collaboration
findings.document_finding: The JLG narrative establishes real Anglican, Methodist and other British liturgical cooperation in the 1960s.
findings.qualification: It supplies no Roman Consilium roster, voted draft or evidence that a group of six Protestants wrote the 1969 Missal.

findings.locator: Benedict XVI, letter of 7 July 2007 accompanying Summorum Pontificum
findings.document_finding: Benedict describes the Roman Rite usages and asserts that the older Roman Missal had never been juridically abrogated.
findings.qualification: A juridical claim in a 2007 pastoral letter must not be read as prohibiting all subsequent papal legislation.

findings.locator: Francis, Traditionis custodes arts. 1–3, 2021
findings.document_finding: The later legislator describes the reform books as the unique expression of the Roman Rite lex orandi and restricts the older books.
findings.qualification: The shift in norm and description must be acknowledged rather than assumed to settle claims about organic development.

findings.locator: Leo XIII, Libertas §§30–35, civil liberty and toleration
findings.document_finding: Leo distinguishes freedom to act according to duty to God from unrestricted religious liberty and permits toleration for civil goods.
findings.qualification: The teaching cannot be collapsed into a universal requirement to coerce all non-Catholics at all times.

findings.locator: Dignitatis humanae preamble and §§1–2, objective religious obligation and civil immunity
findings.document_finding: The Council expressly preserves duties toward true religion while asserting civil immunity from religious coercion within just limits.
findings.qualification: The exact scope of coercion and older civil duties still requires systematic comparison.

findings.locator: Mater Populi Fidelis §§17–22: historical papal uses and suitability of 'Co-redemptrix'
findings.document_finding: The 2025 DDF text reports prior papal title uses and denies that the title is pastorally appropriate for defining cooperation.
findings.qualification: The DDF restriction on an expression is not a claim that Mary's dependent cooperation never existed.

findings.locator: Pius X, Ad Diem Illum Laetissimum, 1904: Mary's dependent cooperation
findings.document_finding: Pius X presents Mary's suffering and association with Christ within the divine economy of salvation.
findings.qualification: The encyclical does not assert that Mary supplies a second independent infinite redemption.

findings.locator: BioLogos 2014 article revised 2021, introductory limits of population genetics
findings.document_finding: The article argues for population ancestry and expressly says genetics cannot prove or disprove the historical existence of Adam as an individual.
findings.qualification: This is a Protestant science-editorial argument, not a Catholic magisterial endorsement of theological polygenism.

findings.locator: Pius XII, Humani generis §§36–37, bodily evolution and polygenism
findings.document_finding: Pius XII allowed qualified discussion of the evolution of the human body but warned against embracing specified polygenist theories.
findings.qualification: Theological original-sin objections and the biological study of population ancestry are distinct questions requiring careful treatment.

findings.locator: CDF, The Message of Fatima (2000), third part manuscript and theological interpretation
findings.document_finding: The CDF published the vision manuscript and theological reflection on the third part of the Fatima secret.
findings.qualification: The publication itself does not logically disprove every claim about private custody or later unrecorded papers.

findings.locator: Irenaeus, Against Heresies V.33, earthly kingdom expectations
findings.document_finding: Irenaeus transmits early Christian expectations of eschatological earthly renewal and millennial images.
findings.qualification: An influential Father's speculative eschatology is not automatically the Church's definitive doctrine of a literal thousand-year reign.

findings.locator: Augustine, City of God XX, interpretation of Revelation 20
findings.document_finding: Augustine distinguishes interpretations of the first resurrection and the millennial interval and discusses the reign of saints.
findings.qualification: The existence of differing Fathers does not establish the acceptability of every modern political millenarian theory.

findings.locator: Humanity+ Transhumanist Declaration points 1–8
findings.document_finding: Humanity+ openly advocates augmentation, future sentience, longer life and moral inclusion, alongside technological-risk avoidance.
findings.qualification: This first-person programme should not be caricatured as advocating coercive abolition of ordinary persons.

findings.locator: CDF 2020 vaccines note §§1–6, limited moral judgment
findings.document_finding: The Congregation allows specified remote material cooperation and states vaccination is not ordinarily morally compulsory.
findings.qualification: It expressly declines biomedical judgment on efficacy and safety and does not approve abortion or all conceivable mandates.

findings.locator: Dorothy Day, Our Stand (1940), Catholic Worker pacifism
findings.document_finding: Day's published first-person argument defends Christian nonviolence amid the Second World War.
findings.qualification: A Catholic pacifist witness should not be attributed to the entire Magisterium as an absolute ban on every just defence.

findings.locator: Marx and Engels, Communist Manifesto Part II, bourgeois property and state programme
findings.document_finding: Marx and Engels call for abolition of bourgeois private property and political class struggle against bourgeois society.
findings.qualification: The document does not prove that each particular state welfare proposal is secretly Marxist doctrine.

findings.locator: United Grand Lodge of England official FAQ, religion and Supreme Being
findings.document_finding: UGLE explains inclusive membership through belief in a Supreme Being, religious pluralism and charitable civic language.
findings.qualification: A self-description is source evidence of an institution's public position, not independent verification of every lodge's conduct.

findings.locator: CDF Declaration on Masonic Associations, 26 November 1983
findings.document_finding: The Holy See says the 1983 Code's omission of the name Freemasonry does not abrogate the negative judgment or membership prohibition.
findings.qualification: The declaration speaks to Catholic membership in Masonic associations, not accusations of individual wrongdoing absent evidence.

findings.locator: Paul VI, Missale Romanum apostolic constitution, 3 April 1969
findings.document_finding: Paul VI promulgated the reformed Missal and described the revision as following conciliar principles.
findings.qualification: A papal promulgation is not the same act as conciliar approval of each later redaction choice.

findings.locator: GIRM 2003, bread-and-wine preparation versus Eucharistic Prayer
findings.document_finding: The GIRM places presentation of gifts before the Eucharistic Prayer and gives those actions differentiated meanings.
findings.qualification: The reform's distinct prayer vocabulary is not proof the Church denied the sacrificial meaning of the Mass.

findings.locator: Ottaviani–Bacci letter and Short Critical Study, 25 September 1969
findings.document_finding: The signatories alleged a grave departure from Trent's Eucharistic-sacrifice theology in the new Ordo Missae.
findings.qualification: This critical judgment must be compared with the precise historical edition and not promoted to binding official invalidity finding.

findings.locator: Paul VI, Missale Romanum: promulgation of reformed Missal
findings.document_finding: Paul VI's act of promulgation is a direct public source that the revised rite was legally issued by papal authority.
findings.qualification: The act does not itself refute every textual criticism or prove that all pastoral results were favourable.

findings.locator: CDW 25 September 2000, GIRM no.299 orientation response
findings.document_finding: The Roman congregation answered that GIRM 299 does not exclude celebration toward the apse; expedit indicates preference, not obligation.
findings.qualification: This reply does not assert that every architecture or local liturgical practice must be ad orientem.

findings.locator: Memoriale Domini (1969), episcopal vote and permission procedure
findings.document_finding: The official poll documents 597 yes, 1,233 no, 315 qualified yes and 20 invalid ballots on Communion in the hand.
findings.qualification: The limited 1969 permission does not prove that 1969 universally abolished Communion on the tongue.

findings.locator: 1917 Canon Law canon 1262 §2 on head coverings
findings.document_finding: Canon 1262 §2 imposed the historical head-covering discipline on women entering church.
findings.qualification: A former universal disciplinary command cannot be projected unchanged into a Code that abrogated it.

findings.locator: 1983 Code of Canon Law canon 6, former-code abrogation
findings.document_finding: The 1983 Code expressly abrogates the 1917 Code and does not recapitulate every old liturgical custom.
findings.qualification: A practice may remain venerable or governed by special norms despite no longer being a universal 1917-Code obligation.
